newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends down, new lows set on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends down, new lows set on weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower and new contract lows were set on excellent crop weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"I can't imagine a situation where we could get much better weather than this present scenario," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man International.
The new contract low for September is $2.43-3/4 per bushel, below the previous low of $2.46 set Friday.
Old crop July collapsed on spreads and hit a session low of $2.59 which is that month's contract low set on January 9.
"The wheat market kicked into July corn. The fact we're getting such huge yields in wheat cuts into feed needs for corn and the July is going down on the spreads," Sernatinger said.
The U.S. corn crop was seeded early this year and the good crop weather led to prospects for bumper yields.

USDA's weekly export inspections report Monday showed U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended June 19 at 27.837 million bushels, within the range of expectations for 25 million to 30 million bushels.
Corn closed five cents per bushel lower to 4-1/2 higher, with July down five at $2.60-1/2.

Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report gave the market little direction. The CFTC said as of Tuesday, non-commercials, including funds, were long corn by about 169.9 million bushels and short by roughly 231.7 million bushels. Commercials were long corn by 710 million bushels and short by 451.4 million.

Cargill Inc bought five million bushels of July and sold 2.5 million December, traders said. Smith Barney sold 2.5 million bushels of July and sold two million September, traders said. Griffin Trading sold three million bushels of December, LIT America sold 3.5 million July and Term Commodities bought two million bushels of September, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 55,000 contracts, below the actual 63,817 traded Friday.

In spread trading, Continental Grain did five million bushels of December/July at 19 to 19-1/2 cents, premium July, R.J. O'Brien did 2.5 million September/December at 2-1/2 cents, premium September and Continental Grain did two million March/December at seven cents, premium March, traders said.

In corn options, ABN Amro-Chicago Corp bought 1,000 December $2.20 puts at 2-1/2 to 2-3/4 cents, sources said. Also, Smith Barney sold 1,500 December $2.50 calls at nine to 9-1/4 cents and Prudential Securities bought 600 December $2.50 calls at 9-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 25,000 contracts, above the 20,591 traded Friday.
